run.runNote: Re-execution of Phase 1 Step 1-2 against the dcnnt-py_vuln source tree checked out at commit 4084ea1 ('Version 0.9.0'), which equals the CodeQL database creation sha - tree and database are now the same snapshot. All file/line evidence below was re-verified against this checkout.

target.projectDescription: UI-less tool to connect an Android phone with a desktop: connection, configuration, plugins, and predefined remote command execution over an encrypted TCP/UDP protocol (JSON-RPC 2.0 payloads).

toolchain.packResolutionExpected: codeql/python-all resolved from the local pack cache by qlpack.yml
toolchain.codeqlExecution: deferred (this step only generates queries; codeql query run / bqrs decode happen in a later step)

scoring.scale: import/package +0.45, route/decorator/annotation +0.30, runtime/bootstrap +0.20, directory/layout +0.05; threshold primary >= 0.75, secondary 0.50-0.74

framework.notes: No web framework detected. All framework scores are below the 0.50 threshold, so no framework reference is loaded. The externally reachable attack surface is a custom protocol stack built directly on the standard library (socketserver + socket + json + pycryptodome). Source/sink shapes below are derived from repository evidence per references/python.md and references/patterns.md (language reference path, since no framework reference matches).
customBoundaryEvidence: dcnnt/tcp_server.py:3 'from socketserver import TCPServer, ThreadingMixIn, BaseRequestHandler'
dcnnt/tcp_server.py:17 'class DConnectHandler(BaseRequestHandler)' - parses 60-byte connection header, decrypts plugin mark, hands control to plugin instance

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: Android clients (paired devices) are the attacker-facing input source. Data enters via (1) TCP socket reads decrypted with a device key, (2) UDP JSON datagrams, (3) JSON-RPC request params consumed by plugin handlers, (4) files written during transfer, (5) CLI args / environment / JSON config at startup. Command execution sinks concentrate in plugin handlers that format config-defined command templates and run them through subprocess with shell=True; in this snapshot none of the template substitution values at those sites is escaped or shell-quoted.

evidence: dcnnt/plugins/notifications.py:45 map(request.params.get, ('text', 'package')) - bound-method form, see uncoveredCases
dcnnt/plugins/sync.py:65 request.params.get('sub'); sync.py:279 request.params.get('path'); sync.py:300 request.params['name']
dcnnt/server_search.py:18 request.pop(...) / request.get('pair') on the decoded UDP JSON dict
dcnnt/plugins/*.py handle_* methods, main() loops, receive_file / receive_file_to_path (base.py:198-204)
dcnnt/plugins/base.py:123 request_raw = self.read(); base.py:148 request = self.rpc_read()
dcnnt/tcp_server.py:97 plugin(app, self, source).main() - hands the connection to a plugin
dcnnt/app.py:83 env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items()}
dcnnt/app.py:111 ConfigLoader(self.environment, path, self.CONFIG_SCHEMA, True).load() - JSON config files
plugin handlers read command templates via self.conf(...) e.g. dcnnt/plugins/opener.py:31 self.conf(('file', 'default_cmd'))

sinkFamilies.evidence: every subprocess execution site in the repository passes shell=True (7 sites listed above)

evidence: dcnnt/plugins/notifications.py:56 cmd.format(uin=uin, name=name, icon=icon, text=text, title=title, package=package) - substitution values from network params (text/title/package) and device records are inserted into the command string with no escaping in this snapshot
dcnnt/plugins/sync.py:316 on_done.format(path=res); sync.py:359 on_merge.format(local=..., remote=..., output=path)

sanitizerObservations: dcnnt/plugins/sync.py:280 / sync.py:288 - target path checked against configured sync paths before use (allow-list style guard, substring containment in ensure_file_syncable at sync.py:331)
dcnnt/plugins/remote_commands.py:40 - command selected by index from the pre-configured remote_commands dict (index is attacker-controlled, the executed cmd string is config-controlled)

No shlex.quote / shell-escaping wrapper is present anywhere in this snapshot: notifications.py (the only file that would import it in a later state) has no quote import, and none of the seven template format sites escapes its substitution values. Sanitizer labeling for pass 2 will therefore likely produce an empty barrier set unless human review adds config-side assumptions.
inputBoundaryInventory.nonVulnerabilityNote: The predefined remote commands feature (remote_commands plugin running config-declared commands selected by index) is normal intended functionality and is NOT automatically treated as a vulnerability; it is recorded only as a candidate boundary for labeling.

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query run (sequential, one at a time) followed by codeql bqrs decode --format=csv; NOT database analyze / SARIF
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist). Raw BQRS output is decoded directly to CSV.
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index, -1 when not applicable)
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs (API::moduleImport(...).getMember(...).getACall()); alias-aware, only genuine resolved calls into external modules
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic module prefix, receiver name); catches dynamic or unresolved shapes that API graphs miss and is subject to name-collision noise

exclusions: no test/fixture directories exist in this repository (nothing excluded on that ground)
logging-only helpers (self.log / logger.*) are not extracted as candidates
pure senders (Plugin.send / rpc_send) are not extracted as sources

uncoveredCases: dcnnt/tcp_server.py:97 plugin(app, self, source).main() - plugin class is looked up dynamically from the app.plugins dict (populated from the PLUGINS tuple); the constructor call target is not syntactically resolvable. Mitigated by emitting the .main() attribute call as an internal_transfer candidate row and by handler parameter rows.

dcnnt/common/jsonrpc.py:130 func(**request.params) - RPCDispatcher looks the callable up in a methods dict and calls it with attacker-controlled params (dynamic dispatch). Not resolvable by extraction; would need a MySummaries taint step if the dispatcher were wired into the live path (currently marked ToDo/unused in this version).

dcnnt/plugins/remote_commands.py:30 / notifications.py:45 / sync.py:131 - map(command.get, ...) and map(request.params.get, (...)) pass bound methods into map(); the element reads are not modeled as call rows. For notifications.py:45 this means the 'text'/'package' values are not captured by the request_param family; the adjacent direct .get calls (:43/:44/:46) and the rpc_read/handler-param families still cover the enclosing function.

dcnnt/common/jsonconf.py:145/187 - string.Template(...).safe_substitute(environment) blends environment/config values into filesystem paths; not emitted as a call candidate (root env/config reads are covered by source families instead).
dcnnt/common/jsonrpc.py:33 type(self).__call__(...) - dynamic self-invocation in RPCError.add_data.

Bare-name (from-import) execution sinks are only matched for distinctive names (system, popen, getoutput, getstatusoutput); bare call/run/check_call are too collision-prone and would need API-graph resolution or import analysis to confirm. In this repository every subprocess site is attribute-qualified (subprocess.call / subprocess.check_call), so this gap is not exercised.

constraintsHonored.notes: No PyVul vulnerability ground truth, CVE patch diffs, or vulnerability descriptions were consulted in this step; candidate families are derived from repository evidence and the loaded language/pattern references only. Project source, database, and Augur installation files were not modified. Only iris/exploration/detection.json, iris/extraction/sources.ql and iris/extraction/sinks.ql were written.
